<thought>We need a SMILES that matches the observed mass (m/z 262.099 [M+H]⁺). The neutral monoisotopic mass is ≈261.092 Da. The formula C13H13N2O4 has a calculated monoisotopic mass of 261.0875 Da, giving a [M+H]⁺ of 262.0948 Da, which matches the observed value within a few millidaltons. Among the isomers returned for C13H13N2O4, the first candidate “C1=CC=C(C=C1)C[C@@H]2C(=O)N[C@@H](C(=O)N2)CC(=O)[O-]” corresponds exactly to that formula (it contains 13 C, 13 H, 2 N, 4 O). Therefore this SMILES is the most plausible structure for the sample. 

<final_answer>C1=CC=C(C=C1)C[C@@H]2C(=O)N[C@@H](C(=O)N2)CC(=O)[O-]</final_answer>
